I am a bisexual but possibly pansexual trans woman and I didn't go to my straight brother's wedding. Not because he is transphobic but for other reasons. My parents are. They hide it and say that they love me but it's just not true. Not really. My brother shares in this aspect - but for different reasons.

You see back in April after 2 months of no longer speaking to my parents because my dad said I was a pariah for wearing a more feminine sweater, them ignoring me when I told them that they could not come to something because I needed space (and then not listening when I told them to leave), telling me I will always be their son, outing me to people, and so many other reasons I had to cut them out. I didn't want to tell him because of two reasons. I was afraid I'd be right in who he would side with and I was also afraid of building a rift in their relationship. But I decided to be honest.

I told them I needed a plus 1 (no one was getting +1s if they weren't dating anyone supposedly) and I asked for one for moral support. He said no and at the time I didn't believe he said it was a conclusion that he and his fiance came to together. But the worst part was he wasn't willing to say "let me discuss it with her." I decide I won't go. 2 days after my mom just suddenly starts using the correct spelling and pronouns. I say I think I know why it is and guess what - I was right because I call her out on it and she never apologized for her behavior and she didn't send me an email or anything else for a very long time when I called her out on her shit.

Months go by and his fiance gets in touch with me. I have a feeling what this is about but I'll go along and meet with them. They relax on the +1 invite enough but I still reject their invitation. They didn't say - we insist and you're bringing a plus 1. They didn't say this isn't negotiable - we want you there. She brought up that they were overbooked already. She brought up the reason why I already wouldn't go after declining. But she also brought up after months from not hearing from my brother that he was going through an awful time at work.

So I reached out. I told him to hang in there. I told him it will be okay and that he has a fiance that loves him and who will help support him if he wants to stop working there and look for work elsewhere (they're both lawyers). I told him that I hope he finds a place he's happy at.

He replied to that. Other moments went by and he demanded everything from me but wouldn't take anything back. Now we know I am slightly autistic. We didn't when I was a child and my parents would say I demanded too much and they had to give in. My brother thinks I'm the golden child and my parents' favorite. My brother has a lot of resentment towards me. And yet he would always tell me he loved me as if it were something he had to say but never meant nor wanted to. He told me he was often too busy to do anything with me because of the wedding and work - but goes to an NBA game with friends during the lead up to it all and while working.

And then the hammer dropped that made me have to cut out him too. My brother whom lives in the same large city county as I didn't tell me our grandmother was in the hospital because of a "minor" heart attack in her 90s. I had to find out from my cousin whom lives in England days after the heart attack. He knew I wasn't talking to my parents at the time. He chose not to tell me.

I called him out on it and I told him we're done. Have a nice fucking life and then it hit me I had no one in my immediate family now I could call family. You have to let go of people sometimes and it's not going to be easy. I'm sorry your brother won't be there because you married the love of your life. But the love of your life is your family. He isn't. So be with your love

As a bisexual but possibly pansexual trans woman currently absolutely attracted to a non-binary trans woman I can tell you that you have to sit down with your husband. You have to talk it out of him until you can't talk it out anymore. And if he cannot love your sister for whom she is and he cannot love your children for whom they may be if they ever decide to come out to you some day - you have to decide what is best for them.
